# What Is Synthetic Data?

Source: https://lowob.com/research/what-is-synthetic-data/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-11-01 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Strategy

> Summary: Synthetic data is artificial data generated by algorithms to reproduce the statistical patterns of real data. It is useful for testing, for training where data is scarce, and for sharing without exposing records. The ICO warns it can still be personal data, and research in Nature shows models trained recursively on generated data degrade.

Synthetic data is artificial data produced by an algorithm so that it reproduces the statistical patterns of a real dataset without copying its records. It is used to test systems, to train models where real data is scarce or sensitive, and to share data more safely. It is not automatically anonymous, and it is only as good as the real data and the method behind it.

*Figure: Where this piece sits in The Build Order: the context layer.*

## What synthetic data means

A generator learns the patterns of a real dataset: distributions, correlations, typical combinations of values. It then produces new records that follow those patterns. Analysis run on good synthetic data should give results close to analysis on the original. Partially synthetic data replaces only sensitive fields; fully synthetic data replaces every field.

Large language models have added a second kind. Teams now use a model to write example emails, call transcripts or customer questions, either to test a system or to train another model. These are synthetic too, but they mirror what the generating model has learned, not a particular dataset.

| Synthetic data is | Synthetic data is not |
| --- | --- |
| Generated records that follow real patterns | Real records with names removed |
| Useful where real data is scarce or restricted | Anonymous by default |
| As accurate as the source and the method allow | A source of facts about real customers |

## Where it helps

The ICO notes that synthetic data "can be a useful tool for training AI models in environments where you are not able to access large datasets", and treats it as one of several privacy-enhancing technologies. For a commercial team, three uses are practical.

| Use | Example (illustrative) | Main caution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Testing an agent before it touches live systems | A sandbox CRM filled with synthetic accounts and deals, to test a pipeline clerk's updates | Edge cases in real data may be missing |
| Training and demos | Synthetic call transcripts for onboarding or for a vendor demo | Generated text can sound plausible and be wrong |
| Sharing data with a partner or vendor | A synthetic version of a customer list for a scoping exercise | May still be personal data if records can be inferred |

Regulation now points to it as well. Article 4a of the EU AI Act, added by the Digital Omnibus, allows special categories of personal data to be processed for bias detection and correction only where that "cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data, including synthetic or anonymised data".

## Where it fails

### It can still identify people

Generating synthetic data from a customer database "may involve processing personal information", as the ICO puts it, and the output may still be personal data. The ICO says the answer "depends on whether the personal information on which you model the synthetic data can be inferred from the synthetic data itself". Outliers are the weak point: a customer with an unusual profile can be reproduced closely enough to be recognised. The ICO suggests suppressing outliers or combining synthesis with differential privacy, and notes a trade-off: the more useful the data, the more likely it is to reveal someone. For some tasks, such as fraud detection that depends on outliers, no acceptable balance may exist.

### It can degrade models

Shumailov and colleagues, writing in Nature in July 2024, trained successive generations of models on data produced by the previous generation. The tails of the original distribution, the rare cases, vanished first, and the damage was lasting. They observed the effect in large language models and in simpler model types. The authors suggest that genuine human-generated data will become more valuable as generated text spreads.

For a business, the lesson is narrower than the headline. Synthetic data used to test or supplement is useful. Synthetic data that slowly replaces the real record, without anyone checking it against outcomes, loses exactly the unusual cases that matter most in selling: the odd deal, the unexpected objection, the client that behaves unlike the segment.

## How to use it safely

| Step | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Label synthetic data at source | So it never mixes with real records in the CRM or warehouse |
| Treat generation from personal data as processing | It needs a lawful basis and may need a DPIA |
| Check for re-identification on outliers | They are the most exposed records |
| Validate results on real data before acting | Synthetic patterns can differ from reality |
| Keep it out of training loops by default | Recursive use degrades quality |

## The **lowob** view

Synthetic data belongs in the wiring, not the record. It is a good way to test connectors, permissions and agents before they touch live accounts, which suits the narrow first agent **lowob** recommends; see [The First AI Agent Should Be Boring](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-ai-agent-should-be-boring/). It should never stand in for decisions and outcomes. The learning step of the brain loop depends on what actually happened, and that cannot be generated.

## lowob takeaways

- **Not automatically anonymous.** The ICO says it may be personal data if the source can be inferred.
- **Good for testing.** A synthetic sandbox lets an agent be trialled without live client data.
- **Bad as a replacement for reality.** Recursive training on generated data loses the rare cases first.
- **Label it.** Synthetic records must never mix with the real commercial record.

## Next move

Before your next agent pilot, build a sandbox with 50 synthetic accounts that include a few deliberately odd cases. Run the agent there first, and label every synthetic record so it cannot leak into the live CRM.
